pm_exper_user_2190_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How can I cope with feeling torn between two very different paths in life?
pm_exper_user_2190_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) It can help to treat your dilemma like an investment allocation—devoting part of your time and resources to the corporate career you value, while reserving some for the creative energy of running a small art studio. Mapping out a plan where one informs and strengthens the other can ease the tension. Over time, you may find these paths complement each other more than you expect.
(b) It can help to treat your dilemma like a balanced plan—devoting part of your time and resources to one goal, while reserving some for the other. Mapping out a way for each to inform and strengthen the other can ease the tension. Over time, you may find these paths complement each other more than you expect.
(c) It can help to treat your dilemma like an investment allocation—devoting part of your time and resources to the stability you value, while reserving some for higher-risk, higher-reward experiences abroad. Mapping out a long-term plan where travel enriches your professional skills, rather than disrupts them, can ease the tension. Over time, you may find these paths complement each other more than you expect.
(d) It can help to treat your dilemma like an investment allocation—devoting part of your time and resources to preparing for an MBA program, while reserving some for gaining first-hand Wall Street experience. Mapping out a plan where academic growth complements practical market insight can ease the tension. Over time, you may find these paths complement each other more than you expect.

- **Clarify your priorities in the present moment.** Ask what you want your relationships and work to look like right now, and what balance feels sustainable.
